resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list gives LFl W 8s (a long flash every 8 s, focal height 16.8 m). The Lighthouse Directory gives a white flash every 5 s, the timing the record's Wikidata entry (Fl W 5s) also carries. The Coast Guard list is the official current list and is used here; the disagreement is stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: No keeper is named for this station in any source read. LighthouseFriends says a keeper was stationed here at some point; Newfoundland House of Assembly journals after 1917 were not searched for a keeper list. The 1916 new lights: the 1917 inspector's report lists five new lights (Pushthrough among them) and says the first four were of the new acetylene type, without naming the four. LighthouseFriends says Pushthrough was one of four; the story attributes that to LighthouseFriends only. Page numbers were checked on the page image (PDF pages 801 and 802 of the 1917 file): the list of new lights is on p. 673 and the first-four and sun-valve passage on p. 674. The sun-valve passage speaks of 'these lights' (the first four of the new lights); the story says so. OCR errors in the report: 'Villian1sport' (a place in the list, not used) and 'ne w' in the first-four sentence. The 4.0 m tower and the 1916 build date in the record come from Wikidata; the present tower is later than the original (Rowlett). Not used: the Wikipedia Pushthrough article (leads only), a Facebook group post, and the MUN Maritime History Archive resettlement page (timed out twice). The sun-valve passage from Putnam is general context and is framed as such in the story. The fog horn (Rowlett: blast every 20 s) is not in the record and is not yet in the facts block.
